newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Sequent CEO backs 97 estimate.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Sequent CEO backs 97 estimate.

text.p: Sequent Computer Systems Inc Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Casey Powell said Monday he was comfortable with analyst estimates the company will earn about $1 a share in 1997 compared with $0.23 in 1996.
On average analysts estimate the Beaverton, Ore.-based company will earn $1.02 a share, according to First Call.

Earlier Sequent announced a contract from Boeing Co worth at least $59 million, its biggest order ever. And the company said it expected to report earnings of $0.20 to $0.23 a share for the quarter just ended, in line with expectations.
"I wouldn't see any reason for analysts to raise their estimates," Powell said.
He said the company remains on track to raise its net earnings margin to 10 percent of revenues and he remained comfortable with projected annual earnings growth of 30 percent or more through 1998.

The company's NUMA-Q 2000 client-server system, introduced late last year, was doing better than expected in both sales and performance. And he added that the company was building a growing backlog of orders, although he declined to quantify it.
The news from Sequent helped drive the company's stock up 1-1/4 to a 52-week high of 25 in heavy Nasdaq trading.
Powell said the stock surge was part of the reason the company has filed to sell 5.25 million shares, an offering that could raise about $125 million for the company to use as working capital.
Powell said the company could complete the secondary offering within a month pending approval from federal regulators.
